subject: Is there a built in way to determine which button was pressed?

messages.author: 5712068fdf482d27
messages.subject: Is there a built in way to determine which button was pressed?
parts:
Say I have an output and it contents depends on which button was pressed. Is there a built in way to determine which button was pressed in Shiny.

Currently if my code looks something like this

a <- someOutput({
  if(input$buttonA == 0 | input$buttonB ==0) {
    return()
  }
  isolate({
    ....some code...
  })
})

there does not appear to be a built in way to detect which button was pressed. I want to produce a different output depending on which button was pressed (I can think of a way to do this). Ideally I can do something like

a <- someOutput({
  if(input$buttonA == 0 | input$buttonB ==0) {
    return()
  }
  isolate({
     if(clicked(input$buttonA)) {
      ....some code...
     } else if(clicked(input$buttonB)) {
       ...some other code
     }
  })
})

messages.author: 2de7c33d05dd213b
messages.subject: Re: Is there a built in way to determine which button was pressed?
parts:
I agree that it would be nice to have such functionality built in.

I usually set an observer for each button that change reactiveValues() object to hold the id of the button pressed. Then use this reactiveValues() object in the output. Do you know any better way of doing it?
